hints.title: Quarter Boundary Interval Confinement
hints.text: Identify products sold strictly within the first quarter of 2019 without any recorded transactions outside that interval.

hints.title: Minimum and Maximum Date Enclosure
hints.text: Group sales records by product identifier and enforce that both the earliest and latest sales dates fall within the target range.

hints.title: Quarter Sales Query Blueprint
hints.text: select p.product_id, p.product_name from Product p join Sales s on p.product_id = s.product_id group by p.product_id, p.product_name having min(s.sale_date) >= "2019-01-01" and max(s.sale_date) <= "2019-03-31".

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name
FROM Product p
JOIN Sales s ON p.product_id = s.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
HAVING MIN(s.sale_date) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(s.sale_date) <= '2019-03-31';
```

complexity.notes: Joining products with sales and computing min and max dates per group runs in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Filtering individual transaction rows with a where clause retains products that also had sales outside Q1.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouped min and max date comparison tests the entire transaction boundary in one aggregation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of HAVING MIN(...) >= date AND MAX(...) <= date to guarantee exclusive interval sales.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def sales_analysis(product: pd.DataFrame, sales: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    grouped = sales.groupby('product_id')['sale_date'].agg(['min', 'max']).reset_index()
    valid = grouped[(grouped['min'] >= '2019-01-01') & (grouped['max'] <= '2019-03-31')]
    return product.merge(valid[['product_id']], on='product_id')[['product_id', 'product_name']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Min and Max Date Aggregation Filter
